capabilities: Sync vault files to Nextcloud, OpenCloud, or CouchDB backends
Push and pull changes via commands with conflict detection
Resolve file conflicts in an interactive keep-local/keep-remote/keep-both modal
Optionally sync top-level Obsidian configuration files
extras: The README cautions that sync can delete or overwrite files, so users must maintain independent backups; it provides no end-to-end encryption and is installed manually from release files.
motivation: The author built it to give users full ownership and privacy over their data by syncing through self-hosted backends.
problem: Obsidian's built-in Sync relies on a hosted service, and there is no built-in way to keep a vault in sync through your own self-hosted server.

requires.name: self-hosted Nextcloud, OpenCloud, or Apache CouchDB server
account with credentials or app token on the chosen backend

summary: Open-source sync plugin that bidirectionally syncs vault files to a self-hosted Nextcloud, OpenCloud, or Apache CouchDB server.
